identity.name: Amaranth
identity.chemical_class: Synthetic sulfonated azo dye (trisodium azo colorant)

function.mechanism: Conjugated azo chromophore absorbs visible light and imparts red coloration; sulfonate groups increase water solubility in beverages and other aqueous foods.

adi.basis: Temporary ADI set in EFSA 2010 re-evaluation and used in later refined exposure assessment.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA did not confirm carcinogenic/genotoxic concern in its 2010 re-evaluation, but lowered ADI and identified potential exceedance in high consumers (especially children) under some scenarios.

fda.notes: Not GRAS for food use; provisional listing for FD&C Red No. 2 was terminated and certificates were cancelled under Part 81.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI range reported as 0-0.5 mg/kg bw.

notable_bans: United States (FD&C Red No. 2 food use terminated/certificates cancelled under 21 CFR Part 81)

concerns.summary: Recent zebrafish study reported dose-dependent developmental and neurobehavioral effects, oxidative stress, and alpha-synuclein-associated changes after amaranth exposure.
Population-level intake modeling in Brazil found that consumers-only and younger groups can exceed ADI, with adolescents reaching up to about three times ADI in worst-case scenarios.

Zebrafish embryo data for multiple azo dyes including amaranth showed developmental toxicity at high test concentrations, though authors noted tested levels were above expected human dietary exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2010 reported no evidence supporting carcinogenicity or genotoxicity for amaranth in the reviewed dataset.
EFSA refined exposure (2013) was mostly below ADI in assessed populations, with exceedance mainly in high-consuming child scenarios.

adi_exceedance.notes: Exceedance appears scenario-dependent: more common under maximum-permitted-level assumptions and in high-percentile/consumers-only intake models.

risk_assessment.rationale: Amaranth has ADI-based regulatory acceptance in EFSA/JECFA frameworks, but ADI exceedance in child/high-consumer groups and recent non-clinical neurodevelopmental signals support a cautionary middle tier rather than risk_free/limited.
key_factors: EFSA temporary ADI reduced to 0.15 mg/kg bw/day
Potential ADI exceedance in child/high-consumer scenarios
US food-use termination under 21 CFR Part 81
No specific IARC group classification found in checked IARC resources
